               <ns0:p n="11">11 How is it, that ye do not understand, that I spake <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> not to you concerning bread, that ye should be ware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the Sadduces.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 Then understood they, how that he bad <ns0:hi>them</ns0:hi> not beware of the leave<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap> of bread, but of the doctrine of the Pharisees and of the Sadduces.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> giving us an account of this passage, <ns0:hi>Chap,</ns0:hi> 8.17, 18, 19. useth some harsher Expre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ions. <ns0:hi>And when Iesus knew it, he said unto them, Why Reason ye, because ye have no Bread? Perceive ye not yet, neither understand, have ye your Eyes yet hardened? Having Eyes, see you not, and having Ears, hear you not? And do you not yet remember? When I brake the five Loaves, amongst the five Thou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sand, how many Baskets full took you up? They say unto him twelve. And when the seven amongst four Thousand, how many Baskets full of Fragments took you up?</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>they said seven. And he said unto them, how is it that you do not under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand?</ns0:hi> Our Saviour here Chargeth them, with three things, <ns0:hi>Ignorance, Vnbelief, Forgetfulness.</ns0:hi> Ignorance in that they did not understand, that his usu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>l way was to Discourse spiritual things to them, under Earthly Similitudes, and so by Leaven he must understand something else than Leaven, with which Men use to Leaven their Bread. <ns0:hi>Vnbelief,</ns0:hi> That they having seen the Power, and Goodness of the Lord and Master, to feed <ns0:hi>four Thousand,</ns0:hi> with seven Loves, and <ns0:hi>five Thousand with five Loves,</ns0:hi> leaving a great remainder, and that he did this for a mixed multitude, out of a meer Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />passion to the Wants, and Cravings of humane Nature, should not judge, that he was able to provide for them, altho they had brought no Bread: Or, doubt whether he would do it or no for them, who were much dearer to him. 3. <ns0:hi>Forget<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fulness,</ns0:hi> which is often in Scripture made the Mother of Un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />belief and Disobedience, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 4.9.23. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 25. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 78.11. There is nothing of Difficulty in the terms, only from this History we may learn these things. 1. That God expecteth that we should, not only hear and see, but under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand. 2. That he looks we should not only hear for the present time, but for the time to come; Christ expected that his Disciple<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> should have learned from his Doctrine, about washing of Hands, that he could not mean the Leaven of Bread, but something else, which might defile them. 3. That he is much displeased with his own People, when he discerns <ns0:hi>Blind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ignorance</ns0:hi> in them, after their more than ordinary means of Knowledge. 4. That former Experiences, of Gods Power and Goodness manifested for us, or to us, ought to strengthen our Faith in him, when we come under the like Circumstances, and a disputing, or doubting after such Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />periences argueth but a little, and very weak Faith, and an hardness of Heart, that the Mercies of God have not made a just impression on our Souls. <ns0:hi>Then understood they that he bid them not beware of the Leaven of Bread, but of the Doctrine of the Pharisees, and of the Sadduces. Mark</ns0:hi> instead of, <ns0:hi>and of the Sadduces,</ns0:hi> hath, <ns0:hi>and of the Leaven of Herod,</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>hich hath made some think, that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> was a <ns0:hi>Sadduce.</ns0:hi> The Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> is reduci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble to two Heads, <ns0:hi>Iustification by the works of the Law,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>those Works too according</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>that imperfect Sense of the Law they gave.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>The Obligation of the Tradition of the Elders</ns0:hi>: Whose Traditions were also (as we have heard) some of them of that Nature, that they made the Law of God of no Effect. The Doctrine of the <ns0:hi>Sadduces,</ns0:hi> we are in part told, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 23.8. <ns0:hi>They said, there was no Resur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rection, nor Angel, nor Spirit</ns0:hi>: These were Principles ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cellently suted to Men of Atheistical Hearts and Lives, and it is more than probable, that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> and his <ns0:hi>Courtiers,</ns0:hi> and some of his <ns0:hi>Lords, and great Captains,</ns0:hi> had suckt in some of these Principles, and these were the <ns0:hi>Herodians</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 22.16. <ns0:hi>& Mar.</ns0:hi> 3.6. These Doctrines are by our Saviour compared to <ns0:hi>Leaven,</ns0:hi> not only because of the sower Nature of it, but also, because Hereticks words (as the Apostle saith) <ns0:hi>Eat</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>doth a Canker,</ns0:hi> and are of a Contagious Nature; as <ns0:hi>Leaven</ns0:hi> doth diffuse its Quality into the whole Mass of Meat. Our Saviour <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.33. had upon this Account compa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />red the Gospel to <ns0:hi>Leaven,</ns0:hi> because by his Blessing upon it, it should influence the World as we heard, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:247" />13 When Jesus came into the coasts of Cesa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Whom do men say, that I the son of man am?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And they said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>2.</ns0:note> Some <ns0:hi>say that thou art,</ns0:hi> John the Baptist, some Elias, and others, Jere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mias, or one of the prophets.<ns0:note place="bottom">This, and the following part of this Discourse, is related both by <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke: Mark</ns0:hi> hath it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8.27. <ns0:hi>And Iesus went out, and his Disciples, into the Town of Cesa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rea Philippi, and by the way he asked his Disciples, saying unto them: Whom do Men say that I am? And they an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />swered, Iohn the Baptist, but some say Elias, and others, one of the Prophets. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.18, 19. <ns0:hi>And it came to pass, as he was alone Praying, his Disciples were with him, and he asked them saying, whom say the People that I am. They answering him, said Iohn the Baptist, but some say Elias, and others say, That one of the Old Prophets is risen again. Matthew</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> name the place, whither our Saviour was going, viz. <ns0:hi>Cesarea Philippi</ns0:hi>: It is so called partly, to destinguish it from another <ns0:hi>Cesarea,</ns0:hi> and partly, because it was built to the Honour of <ns0:hi>Tiberius Cae<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sar,</ns0:hi> by <ns0:hi>Philip</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Tretrach.</ns0:hi> It was a City at the bottom of <ns0:hi>Lebanon,</ns0:hi> and upon the River of <ns0:hi>Iordan. Mark</ns0:hi> saith, this Discourse was in the way, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>As he was alone Praying,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>As</ns0:hi> must there signifie <ns0:hi>after,</ns0:hi> for we cannot think that our Saviour would interrupt himself in Prayer by this Discourse, nor could he be <ns0:hi>alone Praying,</ns0:hi> if <ns0:hi>his Disciples were with him,</ns0:hi> both which <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> s<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ith, So that <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, were cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly translated better. After he had been praying alone, his Disciples were with him, so that this D<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sco<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rse might be (as <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith) <ns0:hi>in the Way,</ns0:hi> before they came to <ns0:hi>Cesarea Phi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lippi,</ns0:hi> whither he was going. <ns0:hi>He asked his Disciples, say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, whom do men</ns0:hi> (or <ns0:hi>the People,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath it) <ns0:hi>say that</ns0:hi> I am? Not that our Saviour who knew the Hearts of all, did not know, but to draw out <ns0:hi>Peters</ns0:hi> following Confession. <ns0:hi>And they said unto him, some say, thou art Iohn the Bap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tist,</ns0:hi> we heard before that <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> said so, others <ns0:hi>Elias.</ns0:hi> This respected the Prophecy, <ns0:hi>Mal.</ns0:hi> 4.4, 5. the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had a <ns0:hi>Tra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dition,</ns0:hi> that before the coming of the <ns0:hi>Messias, Elias</ns0:hi> should come, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.21. <ns0:hi>Some say Ieremias,</ns0:hi> this is only in <ns0:hi>Mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thew,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>one of the Prophets.</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> seeing Christ do such wonderful Works, could not resolve themselves wh<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> he was. <ns0:hi>Herod</ns0:hi> and his Court-party said: That he was <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist risen from the dead.</ns0:hi> They had it seems, an Opinion of some extraordinary Vertues, or Powers, in such as were risen from the dead. Many <ns0:hi>Interpreters</ns0:hi> agree that the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> had an Opinion, that Good mens Souls when they died, went into other Bodies, this made them guess that our Saviour was one of the Old Prophets.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 He saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 And Simon Peter answered, and said, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joh. 6.69. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 11.27. <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 8.37. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.20. 1 Joh. 4.15. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 5.5.</ns0:note> Thou art Christ the son of the living God.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 8. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29. <ns0:hi>Thou art the Christ, Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 9.20. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> answered, and said, <ns0:hi>The Christ of God,</ns0:hi> that is, the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>; you that are my Disciples and Apostles, what is your Opinion of me? Our Lord expects not only <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in our Hearts, but the <ns0:hi>Confession of our Lips, Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.10. <ns0:hi>And Si<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon Peter answered,</ns0:hi> not because he had any <ns0:hi>Priority</ns0:hi> amongst the Apostles, but he was of a more quick, and fervid Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />per than the rest, and so speaketh first, they silently agreed to what he said. What he saith is but little, but of that Nature, that it is the very Foundation of the Gospel. <ns0:hi>Thou art Christ</ns0:hi> the annointed, the Person of old promised to the World, under the Name of the <ns0:hi>Messiah, Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.24, 25. <ns0:hi>the Son,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>by Adoption,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>by Nature,</ns0:hi> for they believed <ns0:hi>Iohn the Baptist, Elias,</ns0:hi> and the Old Prophets, the Sons of God by Grace: It is plain, <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> means more than that. <ns0:hi>Of the Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving God.</ns0:hi> Our Lord had asked, <ns0:hi>W<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>om do Men say that I the Son of Man am?</ns0:hi> And in the same Sense he speaks to the Disciples; Whom do ye say, that I the Son of Man am? Lord saith <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> we believe, that thou the Son of Man art the <ns0:hi>Christ, the Son of the Living God.</ns0:hi> God is often in Scripture called the <ns0:hi>Living God,</ns0:hi> in opposition to <ns0:hi>Idols</ns0:hi> which had Eyes, and saw not, Ears and heard not, nor had any Life in them, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 16.14. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 3.12. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.14. &c. So as here we have a full and plain Confession of that Doctrine, which is the Foundation of the Gospel.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 And Jesus answered, and said unto him, Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-Jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed It unto thee, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Cor. 2.20.</ns0:note> but my Father which is in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord appeareth here to be mightily pleased with this <ns0:hi>Confession</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and the rest of his Disciples, (for we shall observe in the Gospel, that <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was usually the first in speaking, <ns0:hi>Io.</ns0:hi> 6.68.) He pronounceth him <ns0:hi>Blessed,</ns0:hi> and gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veth the reason of it afterward. <ns0:hi>Simon Bar-Iona,</ns0:hi> that is, <ns0:hi>Simon Son of Iona,</ns0:hi> or as some would have it Son of <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> (they think <ns0:hi>Iona</ns0:hi> is a Contraction of <ns0:hi>Iohanna.</ns0:hi>) Our Lord gives him the same Name, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 21.15. <ns0:hi>For Flesh and Blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in Heaven.</ns0:hi> By <ns0:hi>Flesh and Blood,</ns0:hi> our Saviour meaneth <ns0:hi>Man,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Reason and Wisdom of Man.</ns0:hi> Thus it is often used in Scripture, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 40.5. <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 1.16. <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 6.12. Some note it always signifieth so when it is in Scripture opposed to God. Thou hast not learned this by <ns0:hi>Tradition,</ns0:hi> or any <ns0:hi>Dictates from Man,</ns0:hi> nor yet by any humane <ns0:hi>Ratio<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cination,</ns0:hi> but from <ns0:hi>my Father which is in Heaven.</ns0:hi> This confirmeth what we have, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.8. That <ns0:hi>Faith is the Gift of God, Ioh.</ns0:hi> 6.44. <ns0:hi>No Man cometh to the Son, but he whom the Father draweth.</ns0:hi> Men may assent to things from the reports of Men: Or, from the evidence of Reason, but neither of these is <ns0:hi>Faith. Faith</ns0:hi> must be an Assent to a Proposition, upon the Authority of God revealing it. Nor doth any Man truly, and savingly believe, that Jesus Christ is the Eternal Son of God, and the Saviour of the World, but he in whom God hath wrought such a perswasion; yet is not the Ministry of the Word needless in the Case, because as the Apostle saith, <ns0:hi>Faith comes by Hearing,</ns0:hi> and Mini<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sters are Gods Instruments by whom Men believe. No Faith makes a Soul blessed, but that which is <ns0:hi>of the Operation of God.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And I say unto thee that thou art Pe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, and upon this rock I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>And I say unto thee also. Thou art Peter,</ns0:hi> Christ gave him this Name, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 1.42. when his <ns0:hi>Brother Andrew</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ir<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t brought him to Christ: I did not give thee the Name of <ns0:hi>Cephas</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> for nothing (for what <ns0:hi>Cephas</ns0:hi> signifieth in the <ns0:hi>Syriack. Peter</ns0:hi> signifieth in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> I called thee <ns0:hi>Cephas,</ns0:hi> and thou art <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Rock.</ns0:hi> Thou shall be a <ns0:hi>Rock.</ns0:hi> This our Lord made good afterward, when he told him; That <ns0:hi>Satan had desired to Winnow him like Weat, but he had prayed, that his Faith might not fail. Luke</ns0:hi> 22.32. Thou hast made a Confession of Faith, which is a <ns0:hi>Rock</ns0:hi> even such a Rock as was mentioned, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 7.25. And thou thy self art a <ns0:hi>Rock,</ns0:hi> a steady firm Believer. [<ns0:hi>And upon this Rock will I build my Church.</ns0:hi>] Here is a Question amongst In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters, what, or whom, our Saviour here meaneth by <ns0:hi>this Rock.</ns0:hi> Some think that he meaneth <ns0:hi>himself,</ns0:hi> as he saith, <ns0:hi>Io.</ns0:hi> 2.19, <ns0:hi>Destroy this Temple</ns0:hi> (meaning his own Body) God is often called a <ns0:hi>Rock. Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.18. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 18.2. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 31.3. and it is certain, Christ is the Foundation of the Church, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 28.16. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 3.11. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.6. But this Sense seemeth a little hard, that our Saviour speaking to <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and telling him he was a <ns0:hi>Stone,</ns0:hi> or a <ns0:hi>Rock,</ns0:hi> should with the same Breath pass to himself, and not say, Upon my self, but <ns0:hi>upon this Rock will I build my Church.</ns0:hi> 2. The Generality of Protestant Writers, not without the suffrage of divers of the Ancients, say <ns0:hi>Peters Confession</ns0:hi> which he had made, is the <ns0:hi>Rock</ns0:hi> here spoken of. And indeed the Doctrine con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tained in his Confession, is the Foundation of the Gospel. The whole Christian Church is built upon it. 3. Others think in regard that our Saviour directeth his Speech not to all the Apostles, but to <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> and doth not say, <ns0:hi>Blessed are you, but Blessed art thou Simon, Bar-Iona.</ns0:hi> That here is something promised to <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> in special, but they do not think this is any <ns0:hi>Priority,</ns0:hi> much less any <ns0:hi>Iurisdiction,</ns0:hi> more than the rest had, but that Christ would make a more E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minent, and special use of him, in the building of his Church, than of the rest; and they observe, that God did make a more Eminent use of <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> in raising his Gospel-Church, both amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews, Acts</ns0:hi> 2. and the <ns0:hi>Gentiles, Acts</ns0:hi> 15. But yet this soundeth a little harshly, to interpret <ns0:hi>Vpon this Rock, By this Rock.</ns0:hi> I do therefore, rather incline to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpret it in the second Sense. <ns0:hi>Vpon this Rock,</ns0:hi> upon this solid and unmoveable Foundation of Truth, which thou hast first publickly made, <ns0:hi>I will build my Church.</ns0:hi> It is true, Christ is the <ns0:hi>Foundation</ns0:hi> of the Church, and other Founda<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion can no man lay. But tho Christ be the <ns0:hi>Foundation</ns0:hi> in one Sense, the Apostles are so called in another Sense, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 2.20. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 21.14. Not the Apostles Persons, but the Doctrine which they Preached. They by their Doctrine which they Preached, (The Sum or great Point of which was, what <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> here professed) They laid the Foundation of the Christian Church, as they were the first Preachers of it to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles.</ns0:hi> In which Sense soever it be taken, it makes nothing for the <ns0:hi>Papists</ns0:hi> Superiority, or Jurisdiction of St. <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> or his Successors. It follows, [<ns0:hi>I will build my Church.</ns0:hi>] By Church is here plainly meant, the whole Body of Believers, who all agree in this one Faith. It is observable, that Christ calls it <ns0:hi>his Church,</ns0:hi> not <ns0:hi>Peters,</ns0:hi> and saith, <ns0:hi>I will Build, not thou shalt Build.</ns0:hi> The working of Faith in Souls is Gods work Men are but Ministers, by whom others be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve. They have but a Ministry towards, not a Lord-ship over the Church o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> God. [<ns0:hi>And the Gates of Hell shall not prevail against it.</ns0:hi>] That is the Power of the Devil, and all his Instruments shall never prevail against it utterly to extinguish it, neither to extinguish true Faith in the Heart, of any particular Believer, nor to Root the Gospel out of the World. <ns0:hi>The Gates</ns0:hi> is here put for the Persons that sit in the Gates. It was their Custom to have the Rulers, to sit in the Gates, <ns0:hi>Ruth.</ns0:hi> 4.1.11. 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 19.8. neither doth <ns0:hi>Hell</ns0:hi> signifie here the place of the damned, <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, no where (except in one place, and as to that it is questionable, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 16.23.) signifies so, but either <ns0:hi>Death,</ns0:hi> or the <ns0:hi>Graves,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>the State of the Dead</ns0:hi>: Yet, the Devil is also understood here, as he <ns0:hi>that hath the Power of Death, Heb.</ns0:hi> 2.14. The plain Sense is, That our Lord would build the Christian Church upon this Proposition of Truth. <ns0:hi>That he was the Christ, the Son of God.</ns0:hi> That <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> should be an eminent Instru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment in converting Men to this Faith, and where this Faith obtained in the World, he would so far protect it, that tho the Devil and his Instruments should by all means ima<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ginable attempt the extinguishing of it, by the Total Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tirpation of it, the Professors of it, and might as to parti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cular places prevail, yet they should never so prevail, but to the end of the World, he would have a Church, a number of People called out by his Apostles, and those who should succeed in their Ministry, who should uphold this great Truth. So as this is a plain Promise, for the Continuance of the Gospel-Church, to the end of the World.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:248" />19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 18.18.</ns0:note> And I will give unto thee, the keys of the Kingdom of heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth, shall be bound in heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth, shall be loosed in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>And I will give unto thee</ns0:hi>] Not unto thee <ns0:hi>Exclusively,</ns0:hi> that is to thee, and no others; for as we no where read of any such Power used by <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> so our Saviours first Question, <ns0:hi>Whom think you that I am?</ns0:hi> Letteth us know, that his Speech, tho directed to <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> only (who in the Name of the re<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t first answered) concerned the rest of the Apostles, as well as <ns0:hi>Peter.</ns0:hi> Besides, as we know, that the other <ns0:hi>Apostles</ns0:hi> had as well as he the Key of <ns0:hi>Knowledge and Doctrine,</ns0:hi> and by their Preach<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing opened the Kingdom of Heaven to Men; so the <ns0:hi>Key of Discipline</ns0:hi> also, was committed to the rest, as well as un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to him: <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 20.22, 23. <ns0:hi>Whose sins soever you remit, they are remitted unto them, and whose soever sins you retain, they are retained.</ns0:hi> [<ns0:hi>The Keys</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>the Kingdom of Heaven</ns0:hi>] the whole Administration of the Gospel, both with reference to the Publication of the Doctrine of it, and the dispensing out the Ordinances of it. We read of the <ns0:hi>Key of Know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ledge,</ns0:hi> which the <ns0:hi>Scribes</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> took away, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.52. and the <ns0:hi>Key of Government: The Key of the House of David, will I lay upon his Shoulder, Isa.</ns0:hi> 22.22. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>I will commit thy Government into his Hand,</ns0:hi> which is ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plyed to Christ, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 3.7. The Sense is; <ns0:hi>Peter!</ns0:hi> I will be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trust thee, and the rest of my Apostles, with the whole Ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ministration of my Gospel; you shall lay the Foundat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>on of the Christian Church, and Administer all the Affairs of it, opening the Truths of my Gospel to the World, and go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verning those who shall receive the Faith of the Gospel. <ns0:hi>And whatsoever thou shalt bind on Earth, shall be bound in Heaven, and whatsoever thou shalt loose on Earth, shall be loosed in Heaven.</ns0:hi> Some very learned Interpreters think that our Saviour here speaketh according to the Language then in use amongst the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>: Who by <ns0:hi>Binding</ns0:hi> understood the <ns0:hi>determining and declaring a thing unlawful,</ns0:hi> and by <ns0:hi>Loosing,</ns0:hi> declaring by <ns0:hi>Doctrine,</ns0:hi> or determining by <ns0:hi>Iudg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment a thing unlawful,</ns0:hi> that is such, as no Mens Consciences were bound to do, or to avoid. So as by this Text, an Au<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thority was given to these first Planters of the Gospel, to determine (by Vertue of their infallible Spirit, breathed upon them, <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 20.21.) concerning things to be done, and to be avoided. Thus <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 15.28, 29. they <ns0:hi>loosed</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> from the Observation of the <ns0:hi>Ceremonial Law.</ns0:hi> Some think, that by this Phrase our Saviour gave to his Apostles, and not to them only, but to the succeeding Church, to the end of the World, a Power of <ns0:hi>Excommunication,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Absolution</ns0:hi> to admit in, and to cast out of the Church, and promiseth to ratifie, what they do of this Nature in Heaven, and that this Text is expounded, by <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 20.23. <ns0:hi>Whose sins soever you remit, they are remitted, and whose sins soever you retain, they are retained.</ns0:hi> And that the Power of the Church, and of Ministers in the Church as to this, is more than <ns0:hi>Declara<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tive,</ns0:hi> that the Church hath a Power in a due Order, and for just Causes, to cast Persons out of its Communion, is plain enough from other Texts. But that the Church, hath a Power to <ns0:hi>remit sins</ns0:hi> committed against God, more than <ns0:hi>Declara<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tively,</ns0:hi> that is, declaring that upon Mens Repentance, and Faith, God hath remitted, I cannot see founded in this Text. Cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tain it is, that Christ doth not here bind himself to confirm the Erroneous Actions of Men, either in Excommunications, or Absolutions. Nor to Authorize all such Actions of this Nature as they do. I do therefore, rather incline to think that our Saviour, by this Promise declared his Will, that his Apostles should settle the Affairs of the Gospel-Church, deter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mining what should be lawful, and unlawful, and setting Rules, according to which all succeeding Ministers, and Offi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cers in his Church should Act, which our Lord would con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />firm in Heaven. And that the ordinary Power of Churches in Censures, is rather to be derived from other Texts of Scripture, than this, tho I will not deny, but that in the Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neral it may be here included, but I cannot think that the Sense of <ns0:hi>Binding</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Loosing</ns0:hi> here, is <ns0:hi>Excommunicating</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Absolving,</ns0:hi> but a <ns0:hi>Doctrinal,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Iudicial</ns0:hi> Determination of things <ns0:hi>Lawful,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Vnlawful</ns0:hi> granted to the Apostles. The not obeying, or living up to whose Determinations and Decisions, may be ind<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ed a just Cause of casting Persons out of the Communion of the Church: As the contrary Obedi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence, and Conformity to them, a good Ground of re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ceiving them in again. But whether in this Text, be not granted to the Apostles a further Power than Agrees to any Ministers since their Age. I much doubt, and am very prone to believe that there is.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

Luk. 9.21.</ns0:note> Then charged he his disciples, that they should tell no man, that he was Jesus the Christ.<ns0:note place="bottom">We met with some Charges of this Nature before, given to those whom he had miraculously Cured, that they should tell no Man of it, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 8.4. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 9.30. but this seemeth to differ from them. There he only forbad the Publication of his Miracles: Here he forbids them Preaching, that <ns0:hi>Iesus was the Christ,</ns0:hi> a Doctrine necessary to be believed, in order to Peoples Salvation. We are not able to give an Account of all our Saviours particular Actions. 1. We are sure this was a Precept, but of a Temporary Force and Obligation, for we know that afterward they did sufficiently publish this abroad, only for a time, he would not have it published by his Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciples. We cannot certainly determine whether he forbid them. 1. Because they were not as yet fit to publish so gre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t a Truth. Or, 2. Because the time was not yet co<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e, for the Publication of it. Or, 3. He would not have it pub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lished, till he rose again fro<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the dead, having Triumphed over Death, lest People hearing of it before, should have had their Faith shaken by his Death; which seemeth very probable, because in the next Words, he begins to speak of his Death. Or, 4. That he might hereby (as much as might be) avoid the <ns0:hi>Odium</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Envy</ns0:hi> of the Pharisees. Or, 5. That himself might publish first this great truth of the Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />spel, and confirm it by his Miracles.</ns0:note>

                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:248" />21 From that time forth began Jesus <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 20.17. Mark 9.31. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 10.33. Luke 18.31. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 24.7.</ns0:note> to shew unto his disciples, how that he must go unto Jerusalem, and suffer many things of the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and be raised again the third day.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Lord taught his Hearers by degrees, as they were able to hear, and to bear his Instruction. He therefore first instructeth them in the Truth of his Divine Nature, and bring<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth them to a firm, and steady Assent to this Proposition, <ns0:hi>That</ns0:hi> he <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Christ, the Son of God</ns0:hi>; lest they should have this Faith of their's shaken by his Sufferings, and Death, he begin<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neth to instruct them, as to those things, that when they saw it come to pass, they might not be offended, but wait for his Resurrection from the Dead.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="22">22 Then Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Gr. <ns0:hi>Pity thy self.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Be it far from thee, Lord, this shall not be unto thee.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> took our <ns0:hi>Lord</ns0:hi> aside, as we do our Friend, to whom we would speak something, which we would not have all to hear, and began to <ns0:hi>Rebuke him</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> to reprove him, as Men often do their Familiar Friends, when they judge they have spoken something beneath them, or that might turn to their prejudice, saying, <ns0:hi>Be it far from thee Lord. This shall not be unto thee.</ns0:hi> The Words in the <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> want the Verb, so leave us in doubt, whether we should translate them, <ns0:hi>Be Merciful to thy self,</ns0:hi> spare thy self, or <ns0:hi>let God, or God shall be merciful unto thee.</ns0:hi> The last Words Expound them, <ns0:hi>This shall not be unto thee,</ns0:hi> God shall be Merciful unto thee, and help thee, this shall not betide thee. These Words were un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />doubtedly spoken by <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> out of a good intention, and with a singular affection to his Master, but. 1. They spake him as yet ignorant of the Redemption of Mankind, by the Death of Christ, of the Doctrine of the Cross, and of the Will of the Father concerning Christ. 2. They spake great Weakness in him, to contradict him, whom he had but now acknowledged to be <ns0:hi>the Christ, the Son of God.</ns0:hi> Good Intentions, and good Affections, will not justifie evil Actions, Christ takes him up smartly.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">See 2 Sam. 19.12.</ns0:note> Satan, thou art an offence un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to me, for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> thou thinkest that by this Discourse, thou shewest some kindness unto me, like a Friend, but thou art in this an Adversary to me (for so the Word <ns0:hi>Satan</ns0:hi> doth signify) and is therefore ordinarily applyed to the Devil, who is the Grand Adversary of Mankind.) <ns0:hi>Get thee behind me.</ns0:hi> I abo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />minate such Advice, I told thee I <ns0:hi>must</ns0:hi> suffer. It was the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terminate Counsel of God, it is my <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>athers Will. He is mine Enemy that dissuadeth me from a Free, and Chearful Obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience to it. I will hear no more such Discourse. <ns0:hi>For thou savourest not the things of God, but those that be of Man.</ns0:hi> The Word is <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>, and it may be, were better Transla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted, <ns0:hi>Thou thinkest not of,</ns0:hi> or, thou <ns0:hi>understandest not</ns0:hi> The <ns0:hi>things that be of God,</ns0:hi> that is, the Counsels of God in this matter, as to the Redemption of Mankind, thou considerest me only as thy <ns0:hi>Master,</ns0:hi> and thy Friend, and wouldst have no harm come to me: thou doest not mind, or think of me, as the Saviour of the World, or the Redeemer of Mankind, which canno<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> be Redeemed otherwise than by my Death. Tho by thy intemporate Affection to me, thou wouldest hinder the Redemption of Mankind, this is not in this thing to mind, think on, or savour the things of God, but to suffer thy self to be seduced by thy Carnal Affection. It is a mistaken kind<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness to our Friends, to dissuade them for our Personal advan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tage, to do what they cannot do in consistency with their O<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bedience to the Will of God.</ns0:note>
